explanation: Many queries share the same book. Normalize case once per occurrence and accumulate counts in a dictionary, then normalize and look up each query. This pays for reading the book once instead of once per requested word.
correctness: After processing any prefix of book, the dictionary count for each normalized word equals its occurrences in that prefix: inserting a new normalized key starts its count and every later occurrence increments it once. Induction gives exact counts for the entire book. A normalized query identifies precisely its case-insensitive equivalence class; lookup returns that count, or zero when no occurrence created its key. Appending answers in query order preserves repeated queries and their positions.
walkthrough: For book=[Red,blue,RED,green] and queries=[red,BLUE,missing,Red], normalized counts are red:2, blue:1, green:1. The answers are [2,1,0,2]. Red and RED contribute to the same count; the repeated red query does not consume a book occurrence.
timeComplexity: Expected O(B+Q) character work for B book characters and Q query characters, assuming expected constant dictionary access per bounded-length key. Hash-table collisions can worsen this bound.
spaceComplexity: O(D*L+q) storage for D distinct normalized book words of maximum length L and q returned counts; query normalization uses O(L) temporary storage.
edgeCases: Empty book or query array; all queries absent.
Mixed case, repeated book words and repeated queries.
